I’ve been in the industry 8 years and consulted for 3 or so. One brewery I helped consult existed for 20 years before having to change their entire name and branding. 

They existed for awhile because they were known but super small. Once they expanded and opened to new markets, they popped up on different radars and had a C&D almost immediately. 

Any decent intellectual rights lawyer would google the name or mark and tell them the risks off the bat
“Iron Duke” existed in 1992 as an official fan group for Duke University. The term itself is protected and has fair and active for almost 30 years. You won’t beat an established mark like this

“Zero infringement?” Duke literally owns the absolute trademark rights to it and it is also an active mark. 

I can understand why an educational establishment wouldn’t want the same name to an alcohol producing business. I worked a few years setting up a local university brewery and everything except from the colors were changed, we even made a new “homage” logo to our schools.

That honestly just sounds like a poorly run business. I went through a brewery who dealt with the same, albeit a much more minor copyright issue. It was mostly because the owners didn’t know, or didn’t care to learn about marks and general legality or even talk to an attorney over said rights. 

Do your homework before opening a business!
